inputs.sequence_prompt:
A single continuous fifteen-second live-action shot. LOCKED CAMERA attached to the ship, exactly the same framing and viewing direction as this first frame for the entire shot. The camera does not move at all: no pan, orbit, zoom, dolly or change of viewpoint. Keep the same existing deck, red masts, rigging, rail and brass lever in precisely the same screen positions. Do not reveal another section of the ship. Exactly THREE people, left to right: Locke in blue headband on the LEFT, Celes in ivory dress at CENTER, and the ONE silver-haired Setzer at the controls on the RIGHT. Their feet stay in these three original locations. No person enters or leaves, no duplicate person, no additional silver-haired man. Preserve their exact faces, hair, costumes, equipment and body proportions from the image. Natural neutral beige and tan human skin, including hands and ears, exactly matching this corrected frame; steady soft light without pink, purple or red skin illumination.
0-4 seconds: The engines are already humming softly. Only Setzer's right forearm moves as his existing glove nudges the existing brass lever forward a little to its next stop. Keep that same lever, its pedestal and the left-hand control unchanged. A brief mechanical winch sound below the frame indicates the boarding gangway being retrieved. The gangway is offscreen, not an object to create in this frame. The ship and city remain stationary. Locke turns his head down and left to inspect the docking area below him, without walking or turning his entire body away. Celes looks toward Locke, attentive.
4-9 seconds: The winch stops with a firm latch click. Locke raises his face toward Setzer and speaks clearly in Brazilian Portuguese: <d>[Portuguese] Passarela recolhida. Podemos partir.</d> Only Locke speaks. Celes listens and sets her feet slightly farther apart, still in her original central location; her arms stay low beside her dress. Setzer gives a small nod while keeping both hands at the existing controls and his feet planted. No one walks, crosses another body or reaches across the rail. The city remains still until Locke finishes the sentence.
9-15 seconds: The engine hum grows and the ship begins a very slow, smooth vertical lift. The fixed camera, deck, masts, rails, controls and three actors remain in the SAME screen positions, moving together as one solid ship. ONLY the distant city slides gradually DOWN in the background, straight down with coherent rigid architecture; no rotation, no horizontal camera sweep, no bending or melting buildings. Celes and Locke gently shift their weight against the initial lift while keeping their feet grounded; they look out toward the city with restrained relief. Setzer remains the single silver-haired man on the RIGHT, facing forward at his original controls. Mild breeze moves hair and cloth. End during the slow rise, with live small reactions and no freeze or fade.
Keep exactly three intact human bodies visible in the same left-center-right arrangement for all fifteen seconds. No new objects, people or equipment; especially no new wheel. All scenery attached to the ship stays rigid and unchanged. No cuts, transitions, flicker, flashes or glowing effects. Audio is one Portuguese sentence spoken by Locke, quiet engine from start, short winch and latch before speech, engine rising only after speech, light wind. No music, singing, narration or other voices.
